breakfast.name: Banana Pancakes
instructions: Mash bananas, mix with flour, egg, sugar
Cook on griddle with coconut oil
breakfast.description: Banana pancakes cooked in coconut oil.

breakfast.name: Breadfruit Chips
instructions: Slice breadfruit thin
Fry in coconut oil until crispy
Season with salt

breakfast.name: Pandanus Fruit Jam on Biscuit
instructions: Pandanus (the screw pine tree) is a central Marshall Islands food plant
The fruit is dried, pounded, and processed into a sweet, fibrous, orange-red paste
The paste has a unique flavor — tropical, slightly floral, intensely sweet
Mix with coconut cream to loosen slightly
Spread on crackers or flatbread
Pandanus paste is shelf-stable for months — an essential preserved food on atolls
The pandanus trees are planted and maintained by families — ownership of a pandanus tree is important
The sweet paste was historically the Marshallese 'candy' and emergency food
The orange-red color of concentrated pandanus is distinctive
breakfast.description: Marshall Islands' pandanus paste spread — sun-dried screw pine fruit pounded into a sweet, fibrous, orange-red paste and spread with coconut cream on crackers. Pandanus trees are family-owned assets on Marshallese atolls; their fruit is the islands' most important preserved food and natural sweetener. The unique tropical-floral flavor of pandanus has no substitute.

breakfast.name: Spam and Rice
instructions: This requires no recipe in the technical sense — but culturally it's essential
The Marshall Islands has the highest per capita Spam consumption of any country
Spam arrived with American military occupation after WWII (1944)
The canned meat became central to Marshallese diet
Slice and fry, or eat directly from the tin
Serve with steamed rice
The Spam-rice combination is daily sustenance for many Marshallese
Spam-rice appears at every gathering, every family meal
The American military legacy transformed the Marshallese diet permanently
Spam is not seen as inferior food — it's a beloved familiar flavor of home
Other Spam-heavy Pacific nations: Guam, Hawai'i, Philippines
breakfast.description: Marshall Islands' American-legacy breakfast — fried or raw Spam with white rice. The Marshall Islands has the world's highest per capita Spam consumption, a direct legacy of American military occupation after WWII (1944). Spam-rice is not convenience food or compromise food — it is home food, deeply familiar, embedded in Marshallese identity.

lunch.name: Barramundi in Coconut
instructions: Marinate fish in lime and soy
Sauté onion and ginger
Add coconut milk
Add fish, simmer 15 min
lunch.description: Fish in coconut milk with ginger.

lunch.name: Chicken Kelaguen
instructions: Grill and finely chop chicken
Mix with lemon juice, coconut, onion, pepper
Serve with rice
lunch.description: Chopped grilled chicken in lemon and coconut.

lunch.name: Fried Fish with Coconut
ingredients: Fresh lagoon fish (whatever was caught — tuna, wahoo, grouper, snapper)
instructions: The Marshall Islands fishing economy: men fish the lagoon and outer reef by boat
The catch is whatever the reef provides — no fixed species
Fry fish in oil with garlic and ginger until cooked
Deglaze with coconut milk — the coconut milk braises the fish briefly
The coconut milk adds richness and slight sweetness
Season with salt, squeeze lime
The simplicity is appropriate — fresh Pacific fish needs little enhancement
The lagoon fish are fed on coral reef — white, mild, sweet flesh
Cooking fresh reef fish on an atoll, steps from where it was caught
The coconut-lime is the Oceanian flavor signature
lunch.description: Marshall Islands' reef fish in coconut milk — fresh lagoon catch fried with garlic and finished with coconut milk and lime. The fish is whatever the reef provides. The Marshallese fishing economy: men fish the lagoon daily from small boats, and the catch from coral-fed reef fish is exceptionally sweet and fresh.

lunch.name: Turtle (Traditional — Now Protected)
ingredients: Context note — sea turtle is historically important
instructions: Sea turtle has been a traditional food in the Marshall Islands for thousands of years
Turtle soup and turtle meat were central celebratory foods
Since the mid-20th century, sea turtles have been protected internationally
The Marshall Islands has navigated the tension between traditional rights and conservation
Traditional turtle fishing rights are legally protected for indigenous Marshallese in limited contexts
This entry exists for cultural completeness — traditional foods define culture
Contemporary Marshallese celebrations often substitute pork or fish for turtle
The cultural knowledge of turtle preparation is part of Marshallese heritage even if rarely practiced
The ocean around the Marshall Islands is a critical sea turtle nesting area
lunch.description: The Marshall Islands' historically central traditional food — sea turtle, now internationally protected but legally recognized as traditional for indigenous Marshallese in limited contexts. The cultural knowledge of turtle preparation is Marshallese heritage. Contemporary celebrations substitute pork; the cultural memory of turtle remains.

dinner.name: Pork and Taro Stew
instructions: Brown pork
Add onion, garlic, soy sauce
Add taro and coconut milk
Simmer 35 min until tender
dinner.description: Pork and taro in coconut milk.

imageCredit.author: No machine-readable author provided. Thierry Caro assumed (based on copyright claims).

dinner.name: Grilled Fish with Lime
instructions: Score fish, season with lime and salt
Grill until flaky
Serve with coconut cream and rice

dinner.name: Manaba (Breadfruit Chips)
ingredients: Breadfruit (slightly underripe — firmer, better for chips)
instructions: Peel breadfruit, slice thinly — a mandoline is helpful
Fry in hot coconut oil until crispy and golden
The breadfruit should crisp like a chip — it has enough starch
Season with salt immediately from the oil
Cool slightly — they crisp more as they cool
Breadfruit is the Marshall Islands' most important starchy food — planted on every atoll
The chip version is a snack and side dish
Unlike the soft, poi-like preparations (cooked whole), the chip version celebrates the starch content
Coconut oil is the correct frying medium — adds a subtle coconut fragrance
Breadfruit chips are now a commercial product being exported from Pacific islands
dinner.description: Marshall Islands' breadfruit chips — thinly sliced slightly underripe breadfruit fried in coconut oil until crispy, salted immediately. The starch content of breadfruit makes it a natural chip. Every Marshallese atoll has breadfruit trees (a Pacific staple planted by voyaging ancestors thousands of years ago). The coconut oil adds a subtle fragrance.

dinner.name: Jabwer (Preserved Breadfruit)
instructions: Jabwer is the Marshall Islands' ancient food preservation method
Ripe breadfruit is buried in pits, fermented, and preserved for months to years
The fermented breadfruit is sour, pungent, and preserved against scarcity
This was the insurance food for typhoon season — when fresh food was destroyed
The taste is strongly fermented — an acquired flavor
Historically it was eaten during droughts and storms when nothing else was available
Today it is still made and eaten but more as cultural practice
The pit fermentation technique is ancient Pacific technology
Other islands use similar methods: poi (Hawai'i), masi (Fiji)
The sour, pungent fermented breadfruit is distinctly Pacific — no comparison in other cuisines
dinner.description: Marshall Islands' ancient preserved breadfruit — ripe breadfruit fermented in pits for months, the Pacific's equivalent of a storm cellar. Jabwer's fermented, sour, pungent flavor was the lifesaving food after typhoons destroyed fresh crops. Ancient Pacific preservation technology still practiced as cultural memory. Similar to poi and Fijian masi.

dinner.name: Pork Ribs with Taro
ingredients: Taro (peeled, cubed — boil first to remove oxalates)
instructions: Boil taro cubes first until soft — this is essential to eliminate the oxalate crystals that cause mouth irritation
Brown pork ribs in oil
Add onion, garlic, soy sauce
Add coconut milk, taro
Braise until pork is falling off the bone
The starchy taro absorbs the coconut-pork braising liquid
Season with soy
Finish with green onion
This combination (pork + taro + coconut milk) is the Pacific one-pot
Pigs were brought by voyaging Pacific ancestors thousands of years ago
The Pacific pig-taro-coconut trinity is the Oceanian foundational meal
dinner.description: Marshall Islands' Pacific one-pot — pork ribs braised with pre-boiled taro in coconut milk and soy sauce until falling-off-bone tender. The pig-taro-coconut trinity is the Oceanian foundational combination, shared from the Marshall Islands to Samoa to Fiji. Pacific voyaging ancestors brought both taro and pigs across thousands of miles of ocean.

snacks.name: Baked Breadfruit
instructions: Score breadfruit
Bake whole over coals or in oven at 200°C 45 min
Peel, slice, serve with butter or coconut cream

snacks.name: Coconut Candy
instructions: Cook grated coconut with sugar in a heavy pan
Stir continuously
The sugar melts and coats the coconut — continue stirring
As the sugar dries and crystallizes on the coconut, it becomes a crumbly candy
Cool on parchment
The coconut candy is shelf-stable for days
Simple and ubiquitous across the Pacific — the coconut is everywhere
The coconut's natural fat keeps the candy from sticking solidly
Children eat it; elders make it; it appears at every Marshallese gathering
The simplicity reflects the atoll kitchen — few ingredients, total reliability
snacks.description: Marshall Islands' coconut candy — freshly grated coconut cooked with sugar until the sugar crystallizes around the coconut strands. A Pacific-wide sweet (the same idea appears in the Philippines, Polynesia, and Micronesia) because coconuts are universal and sugar makes them into candy. Shelf-stable, simple, and universally beloved.

snacks.name: Coconut Milk Drinking (Niu)
ingredients: Young green coconut (immature — full of water)
instructions: Pierce or open the top of a green coconut
Drink the water directly
The young coconut water is naturally sweet, slightly tangy, and refreshing
A fully mature coconut has less water and more meat — the ratio changes as it matures
On a Pacific atoll, young coconuts are the natural hydration source
The Marshall Islands' most abundant natural drink
Niu (coconut) water is naturally sterile — it was used as a hydration solution in WWII Pacific field hospitals
The coconut palm provides everything: water (young), meat (mature), oil, leaves (roofing), trunk (building)
The Marshall Islands' most culturally important tree
A tree, not a recipe — but the act of drinking fresh young coconut is the foundational Marshallese food experience
snacks.description: Marshall Islands' foundational drink — fresh young coconut water, naturally sterile, sweet, and isotonic. Not a recipe but a way of life: on a Pacific atoll, the young coconut is the most available hydration source. Used as a field hospital IV fluid in WWII Pacific theater. The coconut palm (leaves, water, meat, oil, trunk) is the complete Marshallese tree.

snacks.name: Kilikiti Cake (Celebration Cake)
ingredients: Flour, sugar, eggs, butter (or coconut oil)
instructions: This is a simple butter or coconut-oil sponge cake — adapted from American military introduction
Mix flour, sugar, eggs, butter/coconut oil, coconut milk
Vanilla extract — the Pacific's relationship with vanilla is complex
Pour into a pan, bake at 180°C until done
Frost with whipped cream or coconut cream
The 'kilikiti cake' is the generic celebration cake for Marshallese gatherings
It is explicitly American-influenced — butter cake is not traditional Pacific food
But it's become woven into Marshallese celebration culture through the post-WWII American era
The American influence on Pacific food: white rice, Spam, butter cake, soda — all now 'traditional'
snacks.description: Marshall Islands' celebration cake — a butter-and-coconut-milk sponge, an American-influenced celebration food now woven into Marshallese culture. The American military presence after WWII introduced flour, sugar, butter, and canned goods; these ingredients became the Marshallese celebration vocabulary. American-origin foods are now traditional Pacific foods.

desserts.name: Coconut Candy
instructions: Make sugar syrup
Add coconut, stir until thick
Drop onto tray
Let harden

desserts.name: Coconut Pudding
instructions: Combine coconut milk, sugar, cornstarch in a pot
Heat over medium, stirring constantly
As it heats, the starch thickens the coconut milk
Stir until thick enough to coat a spoon — like a loose pudding
Pour into cups or a flat dish
Cool and refrigerate until set
The coconut pudding sets into a tender, creamy, very white pudding
The coconut milk flavor is clean and rich with no masking
Serve cold — the coolness amplifies the refreshing coconut
Coconut pudding is the Pacific's most universal dessert
It appears in almost identical form from the Marshall Islands to the Philippines
desserts.description: Marshall Islands' coconut milk pudding — thick coconut milk thickened with starch and set, served cold. The purest coconut flavor experience: nothing competes. Almost identical versions appear from the Marshall Islands through Micronesia, Polynesia, and the Philippines — the coconut pudding is the Pacific's universal dessert.

desserts.name: Fried Sweet Potato
ingredients: Optional: sugar, cinnamon, coconut cream drizzle
instructions: Slice sweet potato into rounds or cubes
Fry in coconut oil until golden and caramelized
The natural sugars in sweet potato caramelize easily
Optional: dust with cinnamon or drizzle coconut cream after frying
The sweet potato was introduced to the Pacific from South America before European contact
Evidence of Polynesian contact with South American coast (perhaps around 1200 CE)
The sweet potato's arrival in Polynesia via Pacific voyagers is one of food history's great mysteries
In the Marshall Islands it's a common starchy snack and side
The fried version is sweet enough to serve as dessert
desserts.description: Marshall Islands' sweet potato fry — sweet potato caramelized in coconut oil and optionally drizzled with coconut cream. The sweet potato arrived in the Pacific from South America via Polynesian voyagers (circa 1200 CE), one of food history's great mystery journeys. Now so fundamental to Pacific diets that it's considered indigenous.

drinks.name: Coconut Water
instructions: Crack open coconut
Pour water into cup

drinks.name: Jakaro (Pandanus Juice)
instructions: Extract juice from pandanus fruit
Mix with water and sugar
Serve cold

drinks.name: Coconut Water (Bottled)
ingredients: Young coconuts or commercial coconut water
instructions: The Marshall Islands' most natural drink in its modern commercial form
Fresh coconut water from every atoll — now also sold commercially
Young green coconuts (opened with a machete) are more flavorful than commercial bottles
But commercial coconut water connects the islands to global markets
The Marshall Islands' coconut water is naturally sweet from atoll-grown coconuts
The Pacific coconut variety (Cocos nucifera) is the only coconut species
Atoll-grown coconuts get intense sun and salt-filtered groundwater — producing excellent fruit
Coconut water is naturally isotonic — electrolyte balance similar to human plasma
This is the reason for its WWII medical use
Modern commercial coconut water is a $4 billion global industry originating from traditions like these
drinks.description: Marshall Islands' export drink in modern form — fresh young coconut water, now a $4 billion global industry. Atoll coconuts grown in intense sun on salt-filtered groundwater produce naturally excellent fruit. Naturally isotonic (similar to human plasma in electrolyte balance), it was used as IV fluid in WWII Pacific hospitals. The fresh version from a machete-opened green coconut is irreplaceable.
